name: Mandarin Chinese
notes: The most widely spoken first language in the world. Grammar is genuinely simple — no verb conjugation, no plurals, no tenses in the European sense. The difficulty is the four tones and the characters. Learn Pinyin with tone marks first; the tone is part of the word, not an accent, and mā, má, mǎ and mà are four different words.
syllabus: HSK 1 and HSK 2 in full (300 words) and the first third of HSK 3 — about 425 cards. HSK 3 is where you start to talk about the past, compare things and give reasons; HSK 2 is simple, direct conversation about daily life. Tones matter more than vocabulary at this stage: the guide explains them. Cards can be spoken aloud if Windows has a Chinese voice installed.
